<Warning>Preview, not deployed. The v2 gateway is built but not deployed yet; this call works once the owner deploys `silo-api`.</Warning>

What is this name or id? Companies, funds and listed shares, with their stable ids (CNPJ, ISIN).

Example: `/v2/search?q=petrobras`

Kinds:

- `any`: Resolve a name or id across companies, funds and tickers.
- `company`: The company rows (id_type cd_cvm) of the lookup answer; truncated still says when more than 20 entries matched.
- `fund`: Fund name or CNPJ search, largest latest NAV first. Refuses (over_limit) when more match than the SQL's tier ceiling: narrow q.
- `universe`: The research universe: one row per ticker+ISIN pair of listed shares and units.

`GET /v2/search?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A ticker, ISIN, CNPJ, CVM code, or words of a company or fund name (every word must match, accents and case ignored). Default: empty: list the research universe (kind any or company) or every fund (kind fund, which refuses above its tier ceiling).

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: any: exact ids, then companies, then funds (at most 20 rows). company: the company rows of that answer. fund: fund search, largest latest NAV first. universe: every listed share and unit since 2019-01-02. Default: any.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: Narrows kind=fund to one fund family. Default: all.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind=universe (or an empty q): only the ticker+ISIN pairs whose first_observed <= as_of <= last_observed, dead names included. Survivorship-free. Default: none: every pair the tape has seen.

default.description: The v2 error object. A SILO refusal (over_limit) keeps its message, hint and details verbatim.

What did it trade at? Daily history (split-adjusted by default), latest quote, sessions, indices, B3 FORWARD prints.

Example: `/v2/prices?id=PETR4`

Kinds:

- `history`: api.quote_history: one ticker, oldest first, 1 year to the latest session by default, paged with the function's p_after cursor. With no id: the research universe (the tickers held).
- `latest`: api.quote_latest: the ticker's newest session (raw, adjusted false). With no id: the research universe.
- `session`: One session's quotes from one price view (raw, adjusted false). Paged with order + limit + offset; the default session is pinned in the cursor.
- `index`: api.index_history: one B3 index code (IBOV, IFIX, ...), levels as published (total-return indices, not adjusted). With no id the SQL refusal names the codes held.
- `forward`: api.trade_consolidated_history: one FORWARD-segment ticker; last_price is the close, ref_price is never a trade.

With no `from`, a dated kind reads the last 12 months to `to`.

`GET /v2/prices?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: history: one ticker's daily series. latest: its newest session. session: every quote of one session (the seven price views in one). index: a B3 index's daily levels. forward: B3 FORWARD-segment prints (fixed-income ETFs COTAHIST does not carry). Default: history.

parameters.name: freq
parameters.description: kind history, index, forward. month: the last session of each month, selected from the daily rows (no interpolation; a month with no session has no row). Default: day.

parameters.name: adjust
parameters.description: kind history. split: close_adj (splits, groupings, bonus shares; no dividends). none: the raw close as traded. Every row carries adjusted (true or false); the other kinds are never adjusted. Default: split.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The thing you want: a ticker, a 14-digit CNPJ, a CVM code or a series code. The gateway detects which. Default: none: the resource lists the ids it holds.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the resource's default window, counted back from to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest complete period, from coverage.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

parameters.name: board
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind history, latest, session. A BDI board code (02 is the standard lot). Default: all boards: the series follows the ISIN across boards.

parameters.name: asset_class
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind session. all: api.quotes (standard lot, tpmerc 010). Each class reads its own view (equities, bdrs, units, fund_quotas, cash_securities: standard, odd and block lots, with lot on the row; auctions: tpmerc 017), with every column it publishes. Default: all.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). core: a short set (history: ticker, trade_date, close_adj or close, isin). all: every column the endpoint publishes. index and forward publish few columns, so core is all of them. Default: core.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind session. The session date, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest session in the 14 days to today that matches the other filters.

What did the company file? Income, balance sheet, cash flow, headline figures and every stored version.

Example: `/v2/statements?id=PETR4&kind=income`

Kinds:

- `all`: api.financials: every line, one row per account, latest stored version. Paged by date windows. With no id (every kind): the research universe, whose cnpj links a ticker to its filer.
- `income`: api.income_statements: one row per filed period, with period_months.
- `balance`: api.balance_sheets: one row per filed date. A balance sheet is a point in time, so the source has no period_months.
- `cashflow`: api.cash_flow_statements: one row per filed period, with period_months.
- `headline`: api.company_financials: headline figures per filed period. The function takes no p_doc_type, so period is a selection on the rows' doc_type.
- `versions`: api.financial_statement_history: every stored version of one statement (hidden statement, default DRE), with filing metadata. No as_of: it already shows every version.

With no `from`, a dated kind reads the last 60 months to `to`.

`GET /v2/statements?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: all: every filed line, long (api.financials). income, balance, cashflow: the standard lines, wide. headline: revenue, net income, assets, equity, margins (api.company_financials). versions: every stored version of one statement (api.financial_statement_history). Default: all.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: quarterly: ITR filings. annual: DFP filings. A quarterly filing holds the 3-month and the year-to-date figure; period_months on the row says which. Never add the two. Default: both.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Consolidated and individual are separate filings of the same period; they are never merged. Default: consolidated.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The thing you want: a ticker, a 14-digit CNPJ, a CVM code or a series code. The gateway detects which. Default: none: the resource lists the ids it holds.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the resource's default window, counted back from to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest complete period, from coverage.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). Point in time: only documents CVM received before this date, at the highest version known then. Not for kind versions. Default: none: the latest stored version of every document, which is NOT point in time.

parameters.name: statement
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind versions: the one statement to read (DRE income, BPA assets, BPP liabilities and equity, DFC_MD or DFC_MI cash flow, DMPL, DRA, DVA). Default: DRE.

<Warning>Preview, not deployed. The v2 gateway is built but not deployed yet; this call works once the owner deploys `silo-api`.</Warning>

What is this fund and how is it doing? Profile, NAV, holdings, debentures, FII properties.

Example: `/v2/funds?id=33000167000101&kind=nav`

Kinds:

- `profile`: api.fund_profile: one row per family the CNPJ files under. With no id: the api.funds registry view, ordered by cnpj, paged with order + limit + offset.
- `nav`: api.fund_nav: monthly NAV, quota, quotaholders and flows, oldest first. With no to, the series ends at the family's latest complete period. Refuses above 1000 rows: narrow from, or pin family.
- `holdings`: api.fund_holdings: the listed equities a fund holds (CDA), or with holding the funds that hold a ticker. Paged by date windows.
- `debentures`: api.fund_debentures: the debentures a fund holds, or with holding the funds that hold an issuer's paper. Paged by date windows.
- `properties`: api.fii_property_history: an FII's properties, every filed version, newest first.

With no `from`, a dated kind reads the last 36 months to `to`.

id is a fund CNPJ: 14 digits, punctuation allowed. Find one with /v2/search?kind=fund&q=<name>.

kind=nav columns are per family: a null outside the family's list is not applicable, not missing (coverage?kind=catalog, applicability).

FIDC delinquency (api.fund_nav, panel) starts 2013-01 and is on every row only from 2020-11 (regime break; coverage?kind=catalog lists it under regime_breaks). Through 2020-10-31 a fund with no tab VI row that month is null, not zero and not clean books; from 2020-11-30 it is filed on every row (a fund with none files 0). Never read a pre-2020-11 null as zero or fill it, and never compare a count of reporting funds across 2020-10 -> 2020-11.

`GET /v2/funds?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: profile: one fund's registry row and AUM (with no id: the fund registry). nav: the monthly NAV and flows series. holdings: the listed equities it holds (CDA). debentures: the debentures it holds. properties: an FII's real estate. Default: profile.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: One fund family. kind=nav: the series filed under that family (one CNPJ can file under two). With no id: the registry rows of that family. Default: all.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The thing you want: a ticker, a 14-digit CNPJ, a CVM code or a series code. The gateway detects which. Default: none: the resource lists the ids it holds.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the resource's default window, counted back from to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest complete period, from coverage.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

parameters.name: holding
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). Reverse lookup, instead of id. kind=holdings: the funds that hold this ticker. kind=debentures: the funds that hold this issuer's debentures (ticker, CVM code or CNPJ). Default: none: what the fund in id holds.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). With no id: only registry rows whose status is this, exactly as CVM publishes it (e.g. EM FUNCIONAMENTO NORMAL). Default: all.

<Warning>Preview, not deployed. The v2 gateway is built but not deployed yet; this call works once the owner deploys `silo-api`.</Warning>

What is inside this FIDC? Portfolio, tranches, aging, cedentes, sacados.

Example: `/v2/fidc?id=<cnpj>&kind=tranches`

Kinds:

- `portfolio`: api.fidc_portfolio, newest first. Paged by date windows. With no id: the FIDC registry, ordered by cnpj.
- `tranches`: api.fidc_tranches: per series, quota value, quotaholders and returns. Paged by date windows.
- `aging`: api.fidc_aging: the to_maturity, overdue and overdue_total ladders. Paged by date windows.
- `cedentes`: api.fidc_cedentes: the originators a fund buys from, or with cedente the funds that buy from one. Paged by date windows.
- `sacados`: api.fidc_sacados: the largest debtors, as anonymized ranks (there is no debtor-side lookup). Paged by date windows.

With no `from`, a dated kind reads the last 24 months to `to`.

id is a FIDC CNPJ: 14 digits, punctuation allowed. With no id, kind=portfolio lists the FIDC registry (api.funds, entity_type fidc).

FIDC delinquency (api.fund_nav, panel) starts 2013-01 and is on every row only from 2020-11 (regime break; coverage?kind=catalog lists it under regime_breaks). Through 2020-10-31 a fund with no tab VI row that month is null, not zero and not clean books; from 2020-11-30 it is filed on every row (a fund with none files 0). Never read a pre-2020-11 null as zero or fill it, and never compare a count of reporting funds across 2020-10 -> 2020-11.

Tab X (the SCR grade ladders of kind=portfolio) is filed from 2023-10: earlier months have no scr rows, not zero-graded ones. Values are as filed.

`GET /v2/fidc?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: portfolio: the receivables book, long (tab II sectors, tab X SCR ladders, tax debt). tranches: each senior and subordinated series. aging: the to-maturity and overdue ladders. cedentes: the originators it buys from. sacados: its largest debtors, as anonymized ranks. Default: portfolio.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The thing you want: a ticker, a 14-digit CNPJ, a CVM code or a series code. The gateway detects which. Default: none: the resource lists the ids it holds.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the resource's default window, counted back from to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest complete period, from coverage.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

parameters.name: series
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind=tranches: one TAB_X_CLASSE_SERIE, matched exactly as filed. Default: all.

parameters.name: cedente
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind=cedentes, instead of id: the funds that buy from this originator (CPF or CNPJ, or a listed ticker or CVM code). Default: all.

parameters.name: item
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind=portfolio: one part of the book, matched against the row's kind column: sector (tab II), scr_debtor or scr_operation (tab X ladders), tax_debt. Default: all.

get.description:
<Warning>Preview, not deployed. The v2 gateway is built but not deployed yet; this call works once the owner deploys `silo-api`.</Warning>

Options, termo and futures: chains, histories, exercises, the DI1 settlement.

Example: `/v2/derivatives?id=PETR&kind=chain`

Kinds:

- `chain`: api.option_chain: calls and puts of one prefix on one session, by expiry, strike, side. One call holds the chain, served in pages; a chain the SQL may have cut (199 anonymous, 1,000 rows) is refused.
- `history`: api.option_history: one option code's daily quotes, oldest first. Refuses above 1000 rows: narrow from/to.
- `exercises`: api.option_exercises: exercise prints for a prefix, oldest first. Paged by date windows; a window the SQL may have cut is halved.
- `termo`: api.termo_history: one termo code's daily quotes, oldest first. Refuses above 1000 rows: narrow from/to.
- `futures`: api.future_series: one DI1, DOL or WDO contract through time, oldest first. Refuses above 1000 rows.
- `futures_curve`: api.future_curve: every contract of a root (id, default DI1) on one session, nearest first.
- `di_settlement`: api.di_settlement (a GET view): DI1 settlement rate, previous rate, open interest per session and contract, newest first. With no id, every contract, paged with order + limit + offset.

With no `from`, a dated kind reads the last 12 months to `to`.

id per kind: chain and exercises take an option prefix (at least 3 characters, e.g. PETR); history and termo one B3 code (codneg); futures one outright contract (DI1F27, DOLF27); futures_curve a root (DI1, DOL or WDO; none: DI1); di_settlement one DI1 contract (none: every contract).

chain and exercises are cut by the SQL at a tier ceiling without saying so, so the gateway asks for 1,001 rows: a count equal to a tier ceiling (chain 200 or 2000, exercises 500 or 5000, or PostgREST's 1000) or above 1,000 cannot be told from a cut. chain refuses it (over_limit); exercises halves its date window and tries again, and refuses only a single day that is still cut.

Exercises are exercise events, not quotes. DI1 rates are % a.a. on 252 business days, as B3 settles them; nothing is derived.

`GET /v2/derivatives?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: chain: one session's option chain for a prefix. history: one option's daily quotes. exercises: option exercise events for a prefix. termo: one forward (termo) code's quotes. futures: one futures contract's daily settlement. futures_curve: every contract of a root on one session. di_settlement: DI1 settlement rates per session and contract. Default: chain.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: kind chain and futures_curve: the B3 session, YYYY-MM-DD. A date with no session returns no rows. Default: the latest session held (chain: the newest option session; futures_curve: the root's newest session).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The thing you want: a ticker, a 14-digit CNPJ, a CVM code or a series code. The gateway detects which. Default: none: the resource lists the ids it holds.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the resource's default window, counted back from to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest complete period, from coverage.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

parameters.name: expiry_from
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind chain: only series expiring on or after this date. Default: today (the SQL's CURRENT_DATE): expired series are left out.

default.description: The v2 error object. A SILO refusal (over_limit) keeps its message, hint and details verbatim.

<Warning>Preview, not deployed. The v2 gateway is built but not deployed yet; this call works once the owner deploys `silo-api`.</Warning>

What does the rate curve look like? B3 reference curves, their history and vertices.

Example: `/v2/curves?curve=PRE`

Kinds:

- `snapshot`: api.curve: one curve on one session, shortest vertex first, fixed and moving vertices with rate_basis.
- `history`: api.curve_history: one fixed vertex through time, oldest first. Refuses above 1000 rows: narrow from/to.
- `vertices`: api.reference_rate (a GET view): one curve's vertices on one session (business_days, calendar_days, rate_pct as published). Paged with order + limit + offset; the default session is pinned in the cursor.

With no `from`, a dated kind reads the last 12 months to `to`.

PRE and DPL are % a.a. on 252 business days; DOC is % a.a. linear on 360 calendar days, so its vertices under about 30 calendar days are not a rate level. rate_basis rides on every snapshot and history row.

Past the last maturity of the anchoring contract (DI1, DDI, DAP) B3 extrapolates: the long vertices are not prices. Nothing is interpolated: a tenor that is not one of B3's fixed vertices is refused with the list.

`GET /v2/curves?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: snapshot: one curve on one session, every vertex, with its rate basis. history: one fixed vertex through time. vertices: the raw reference-rate rows (api.reference_rate) of one curve on one session. Default: snapshot.

parameters.name: curve
parameters.description: PRE: DI x pre. DOC: the clean onshore dollar coupon. DPL: the clean IPCA coupon (a real rate). Default: PRE.

parameters.name: tenor
parameters.description: kind history: the nominal tenor of one of B3's fixed vertices, in CALENDAR days (B3's vertex_code: 1, 30, 60, 90, ... 360, 720, ... 10800). 360 is the one-year vertex. Any other tenor is refused with the list, never interpolated. Default: 360.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: First date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the resource's default window, counted back from to.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest complete period, from coverage.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). kind snapshot and vertices: the B3 session, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the newest session held for the curve (vertices: the newest in the 14 days to today).

<Warning>Preview, not deployed. The v2 gateway is built but not deployed yet; this call works once the owner deploys `silo-api`.</Warning>

Macro series, inflation and its item tree, PTAX, Focus expectations.

Example: `/v2/macro?kind=inflation`

Kinds:

- `series`: api.macro_series: one SGS series by label or code, oldest first. Refuses above 1000 rows: narrow from/to.
- `inflation`: api.inflation: the IPCA set by month with acc_12m, 3 years by default. Refuses above 1000 rows: pin id or family, or narrow from.
- `inflation_items`: api.inflation_items: IBGE's IPCA tree (weight, monthly change, contribution, year-to-date and 12-month change), 3 years by default. With no id, the groups (level 1); with an id, that item at its own level.
- `fx`: api.ptax: one currency's PTAX, BRL per one unit, as published. currency=all reads the api.ptax_daily view, every currency at once.
- `expectations`: api.focus_expectations: one survey and horizon across survey dates (the weekly revision path), median, mean and standard deviation. Refuses above 1000 rows.

With no `from`, a dated kind reads the last 12 months to `to`.

id per kind: series takes a label or SGS code (SELIC_META, CDI, IGPM, 432); inflation one series label (IPCA, IPCA_CORE_EX0, ...; none: every series); inflation_items an IBGE structure number or SIDRA item code (none: the groups); expectations a Focus indicator (IPCA, Selic, ...; none: every indicator).

BACEN's IPCA group codes 1640-1643 are Comunicação, Saúde, Despesas pessoais, Educação, as measured against SIDRA. Focus rows are baseCalculo=0 (the trailing 30-day sample); the 12-month inflation survey is unsmoothed. Nothing is filled.

`GET /v2/macro?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: series: one BACEN SGS series. inflation: the IPCA set (headline, cores, groups, diffusion) with 12-month accumulation. inflation_items: IBGE's IPCA item tree with weights. fx: BACEN PTAX buy and sell rates. expectations: the BCB Focus survey path. Default: series.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Last date of the window, YYYY-MM-DD. Default: the latest complete period, from coverage.

parameters.name: limit

Who is short, lending or flowing in? Short interest, lending trades and brokers, investor flow.

Example: `/v2/positioning?id=PETR4`

Kinds:

- `short_interest`: api.short_interest (a GET view), newest first. With no id, every ticker, paged with order + limit + offset.
- `short_by_sector`: api.short_interest_by_sector (a GET view), newest first.
- `lending`: api.lending_trades (a GET view): count, quantity, rates and how many brokers stood on each leg, newest first.
- `lending_brokers`: api.lending_participants (a GET view): per broker, quantity lent, borrowed and net, and how much it crossed its own clients, newest first.
- `investor_flow`: api.investor_flow (a GET view): buy, sell and net by investor type, newest first.

With no `from`, a dated kind reads the last 3 months to `to`.

B3 keeps about 21 business days of the lending book and publishes no archive: history starts when SILO began capturing, and a missed session is lost, not late.

Short interest reads only B3's own Total rows of the open-position book (is_total), never the per-market rows added up. Read pct_float with float_basis: index_free_float and shares_outstanding are different denominators.

lending_brokers: the broker is the B3 participant on the leg (doador / tomador), not the beneficial owner; about 75% of trades carry the same broker on both legs. Never read a large borrow as the broker being short.

investor_flow is in R$ thousands, differenced from B3's month-to-date snapshots; a row with flow_basis unknown_opening_snapshot carries null flows on purpose.

`GET /v2/positioning?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

Which funds look odd? Forensic screens: signals, not verdicts.

Example: `/v2/screens`

Kinds:

- `list`: The screens, one line each, with the family each reads and its SQL defaults (from api.catalog().screens).
- `captive_vehicles`: FIIs whose NAV peaked above min_aum while the quotaholder count never reached max_investors.
- `delinquency_drivers`: FIDC delinquency, first vs last observation in BRL and in points of NAV, the move classified (driver). No window before 2025-01.
- `dormant_funds`: FI classes that filed every month of the window with zero subscriptions and zero redemptions (empty_shell, parked_capital).
- `dormant_trend`: dormant_funds counted at every month-end: funds filing, empty shells, parked capital and its NAV.
- `evergreen_aging`: FIDCs whose receivables overdue more than 1080 days stay a large, nearly constant share of delinquency.
- `late_filers`: FIIs and FIDCs whose monthly informe reached FNET at least min_days_late days after the cited deadline, in at least min_late months.
- `overdue_securit`: CRI, CRA and other series past their filed maturity whose newest filing still reports a non-terminal status.
- `restatements`: Funds whose FNET re-filings (versao > 1) in the window reach min_restatements and min_rate_pct of their documents.
- `silent_filers`: Funds CVM still lists as active whose last periodic informe is min_silent_months to max_silent_months behind their family.
- `zombie_growth`: FIDCs with delinquency above min_delinq_pct of NAV while NAV stays above min_aum, in one aging month.

Signal, not a verdict: a screen lists a pattern worth a look. Legal funds match every screen (exclusive vehicles, wind-downs, distressed mandates, routine corrections). Every response repeats this in meta.signal.

Each threshold is hidden and defaults to the SQL function's own default; meta.request echoes the value applied. A threshold the chosen screen does not take is bad_request.

`GET /v2/screens?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: list (the default, no kind given): the screens, one line each, with their defaults. Any other value runs that screen (api.screen_<kind>). Default: list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). zombie_growth: the aging month-end (p_period). delinquency_drivers, restatements, late_filers: the window end (p_end). Default: the screen's own: zombie_growth the latest aging month; delinquency_drivers the latest complete FIDC month; restatements today; late_filers the newest month whose deadline has passed.

parameters.name: months
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). delinquency_drivers (2..24), restatements, late_filers (1..36): the window length in months. Default: the screen's SQL default (12).

parameters.name: lookback_months
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). captive_vehicles, evergreen_aging, dormant_funds, dormant_trend: the trailing window in months. Default: the screen's SQL default: captive_vehicles 3, evergreen_aging 12, dormant_funds 3, dormant_trend 3.

parameters.name: history_months
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). dormant_trend: month-ends emitted, 1..60. Default: the SQL default (36).

parameters.name: min_months
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). delinquency_drivers: observations a fund needs, 2..months. Default: the SQL default (6).

parameters.name: min_aum
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). zombie_growth, captive_vehicles: the NAV floor, BRL. Default: the screen's SQL default: zombie_growth 1000000, captive_vehicles 50000000 (BRL).

parameters.name: min_nav
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). dormant_funds: keep rows whose last NAV is at least this, BRL (an output filter). Default: none: no floor.

parameters.name: min_delinq_pct
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). zombie_growth: delinquency floor, percent of NAV, 0..100. Default: the SQL default (5).

parameters.name: max_investors
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). captive_vehicles: flagged when the window minimum quotaholder count is below this, 1..1000. Default: the SQL default (10).

parameters.name: min_longtail_pct
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). evergreen_aging: share of delinquency overdue more than 1080 days, 0..100. Default: the SQL default (70).

parameters.name: max_variation_pp
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). evergreen_aging: largest move of that share across the window, percentage points. Default: the SQL default (10).

parameters.name: min_volume
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). overdue_securit: paid-in volume floor, BRL. Default: the SQL default (100000).

parameters.name: min_delta_brl
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). delinquency_drivers: the up/down threshold on delinquency, BRL. Default: the SQL default (1000000).

parameters.name: min_delta_pp
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). delinquency_drivers: the up/down threshold on the rate, percentage points. Default: the SQL default (1.0).

parameters.name: min_restatements
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). restatements: re-filings (versao > 1) in the window, 1..1000. Default: the SQL default (3).

parameters.name: min_rate_pct
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). restatements: re-filings as percent of the fund's documents in the window, 0..100. Default: the SQL default (20).

parameters.name: min_days_late
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). late_filers: days past the cited deadline that count as late, 1..90. Default: the SQL default (5).

parameters.name: min_late
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). late_filers: late months a fund needs in the window. Default: the SQL default (2).

parameters.name: min_silent_months
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). silent_filers: complete months with no filing, 1..120. Default: the SQL default (3).

parameters.name: max_silent_months
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). silent_filers: and at most this many, up to 240. Default: the SQL default (24).

parameters.name: dormancy
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). dormant_funds: keep one dormancy (an output filter). empty_shell: no quotaholder. parked_capital: quotaholders, no flow. Default: all.

parameters.name: driver
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). delinquency_drivers: keep one class of move (an output filter). Default: all.

parameters.name: modality
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). restatements: count only one FNET modalidade. RE: voluntary. RC: required by CVM. Default: all.

parameters.name: family
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). late_filers (fii, fidc) and silent_filers (fi, fidc, fii, fiagro): keep one family (an output filter). Default: all.

Diagnose a portfolio: resolve statement lines, fees, look-through, movement (POST).

Example: `POST /v2/portfolio?kind=resolve {"names": ["ITAU RF DI"]}`

Kinds:

- `resolve`: api.portfolio_resolve: up to 5 ranked candidate funds per statement line (a printed CNPJ wins, then an ETF ticker, an exact name, a trigram match).
- `fees`: api.portfolio_fees: the disclosed fee and the fee estimated from the balancete, never mixed.
- `fee_peers`: api.portfolio_fee_peers: the admin fee against funds and ETFs of the same filed class, one row per CNPJ.
- `lookthrough`: api.portfolio_lookthrough: one CDA month, holdings followed through fund quotas up to max_depth levels.
- `movement`: api.portfolio_movement: the fund's monthly quota return against its filed class (movimento incomum).
- `instruments`: api.portfolio_instruments: CRA, CRI and debenture codes matched to their series, one line per code.
- `fund_terms`: api.portfolio_fund_terms: manager, administrator and redemption terms as filed, one line per CNPJ.
- `equivalents`: api.portfolio_equivalents: the active ETFs tracking an index the owner-reviewed list maps to each filed class.
- `debenture_returns`: api.portfolio_debenture_returns: 13 month-ends of median fund marks (CDA block 4) per debenture ticker; marks, not trades. Needs month.

A data call is a POST: kind, month and the hidden parameters go in the query string, the lists go in a JSON body (see body). ?help stays a GET. Read-only: every kind is one api.portfolio_* function.

Each list is capped by its function (200 entries, 70 for debenture_returns, 50 classes for equivalents) and refused above it, never trimmed.

Not served: portfolio_credit_returns (held back with the ANBIMA-linked endpoints). The class in fees, fee_peers, movement and equivalents is the ANBIMA class label as filed in the CVM Extrato; no ANBIMA table is read.

`GET /v2/portfolio?help` describes the main parameters, `?help=all` adds the hidden ones.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: resolve: statement lines to candidate funds. fees: estimated and disclosed fees. fee_peers: the admin fee against its filed class. lookthrough: holdings through fund quotas. movement: the month's quota return against its class. instruments: CRA, CRI and debenture codes. fund_terms: manager, administrator, redemption terms. equivalents: the ETFs that track a class's index. debenture_returns: 13 month-ends of debenture marks. Default: resolve.

parameters.name: month
parameters.description: Any day of the month. fees, lookthrough, movement: the month read. debenture_returns: the window's last month. Default: the latest complete month, as each function defines it (fees: each fund's newest balancete; lookthrough: the last complete CDA month; movement: the last complete FI month). debenture_returns has no default month and needs one.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size. More rows than one page come through next_page_url, never cut silently; a call stops at the tier's rows-per-call cap with meta.tier_cap_reached. Default: the tier's page maximum (10 anonymous, 100 signed in); a larger value is coerced to it.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The opaque cursor from a previous next_page_url. It carries every other parameter: send it alone (another parameter with a different value is bad_request). Default: none: the first page.

parameters.name: max_depth
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). lookthrough: fund-quota levels looked through, 1..6 (the SQL default is 4). Default: 4.

parameters.name: as_of
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). fee_peers: dates the comparison and excludes later documents; it reads the latest Extrato, so it is not a historical backtest. equivalents: snapshots dated after it are not read. Default: today (the SQL default).

parameters.name: max_monthly_drop_pct
parameters.description: Hidden parameter (`?help=all` lists it). debenture_returns: a monthly PU drop beyond this is flagged queda_pu_possivel_evento. Default: none: every decrease is flagged limite_pendente (the threshold is the owner's to set).

default.description: The v2 error object. A SILO refusal (over_limit) keeps its message, hint and details verbatim.

requestBody.description: A JSON object of lists. Every other parameter goes in the query string.

id.description: The list: fund CNPJs (fees, fee_peers, lookthrough, movement, fund_terms; resolve: the CNPJ each line prints, parallel to names), instrument codes (instruments), filed ANBIMA class labels (equivalents) or debenture tickers (debenture_returns). Null entries are allowed where the function takes them. Default: none: required by every kind except resolve.

names.description: resolve: one statement line each, the fund name as printed. Default: none: required by resolve.

quotas.description: resolve: the quota value each line prints, parallel to names, for the tie-break. Default: none.

quota_dates.description: resolve: the date each quota refers to, parallel to names. Default: none.
